This response follows reports from Cambodian media framing the release as a 'great victory' for Phnom Penh. The center emphasized that the move does not impact Thai sovereignty and was not part of any secret exchange or conditions.

titleEn: 2nd Army Region reveals no border clashes but Cambodia is reinforcing troops

He urged both nations to resolve issues through technical and legal mechanisms as agreed upon during the General Border Committee (GBC) meeting.

titleEn: Cambodia emphasizes it won't accept border changes made through force

title: Thai-Cambodia border calm on Jan 1, but reinforcements and drone activity spotted

titleEn: Thai-Khmer relations 'will never be the same,' former Intel chief advises NSC to set new stance

He stated that Cambodia had actually encroached on Thai territory for over 40 years with state support. The current military presence is to 'organize' and restore order in areas that were illegally occupied by Cambodian settlements and military posts.
title: กองทัพบกโต้สื่อระดับโลก บิดเบือนข้อมูลไทยรุกรานกัมพูชา ยืนยันพื้นที่ควบคุมอยู่ในอธิปไตยไทย

The detainees stated they fled Cambodia due to extreme hardship, lack of food, and unemployment, risking their lives to find work in Thailand to survive.
title: ฉก.นย.จันทบุรี จับ 67 ชาวกัมพูชา หนีความอดอยาก-ไม่มีงานทำ เข้าไทย
titleEn: Chanthaburi Navy task force arrests 67 Cambodians fleeing famine and unemployment

summary: Air Marshal Prapas Sornjaidee, director of the joint press center for the Thai-Cambodian border situation, strictly denied Cambodia's allegations of territorial encroachment following the ceasefire. He stated that Thailand respects international law, the UN Charter, and the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) framework. The statement follows Cambodian claims that Thai forces occupied areas in four provinces and dismantled civilian structures.
title: ไทยปัดรุกล้ำดินแดนกัมพูชา ย้ำเคารพอธิปไตยของทุกประเทศ
titleEn: Thailand denies encroaching on Cambodian territory, insists on respecting sovereignty

Shipping containers and barbed wire have been installed as temporary barriers. The military claims these areas have been under Cambodian occupation for 40 years, and local Thai farmers are now regaining their land. Meanwhile, Cambodia's spokesperson warned they will not accept border changes by force.
title: Govt denies 'land grab'

summary: Government spokesperson Pen Bona clarified that unilateral Thai actions like placing containers or raising flags do not constitute legal evidence of a border. He reaffirmed Cambodia's commitment to the Franco-Siamese treaties and maps. Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata added that the military is monitoring the ceasefire implementation by the Thai side, noting it is a shared responsibility.
title: Cambodia Reaffirms Official Border with Thailand, Rejects Unilateral Actions

The report claims anti-tank rockets similar to those seized in previous clashes were spotted. Officials noted that while the situation is under control, the military remains on high alert for any escalation.
title: Army Region 2 Releases Video of Cambodian Buildup at Preah Vihear

summary: Cambodian authorities repatriated 162 Thai nationals through the Ban Laem permanent border checkpoint in Chanthaburi. The group had been detained in Siem Reap. Initial screenings by Thai authorities found 6 individuals with outstanding warrants, who were taken into custody for legal processing, while others undergo standard screening and assistance procedures.
title: กัมพูชาส่งตัว 162 คนไทยกลับประเทศ หลังถูกกักตัวในเมืองเสียมราฐ

Organizers had been monitoring the Thai-Cambodian border conflict closely as Buriram is near the border and the Chang International Circuit was briefly used as a temporary shelter. Authorities assured that the situation is easing and will not affect the event.

The Thai source uses highly emotional and biased language.

summary: The border situation remains 'operationally quiet but security-tense.' About 62.5% of respondents perceive the current relationship as 'conflicting.' The top concern identified by 41.6% of participants is the protection of sovereignty and the prevention of threats to the country, followed by solving the issue of call center scams based in Cambodia.
title: Poll: 53.5% of Bangkok Residents Say Thai-Cambodia Policy Impacts Their Vote

Thailand urges the international community to verify facts over rhetoric.

Thailand claims to have evidence of Cambodian forces long occupying Thai territory illegally.
title: Thailand accuses Cambodia of war crimes

Thailand remains committed to resolving the border dispute through the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) rather than force.

titleEn: Clarification of Allegations Made by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Cambodia

Residents were pictured waving flags to thank the departing troops. Thailand insists it is acting within its sovereignty and using direct communication channels to resolve disputes.

titleEn: Thai military urges Cambodia to stop provocative communication, violating ceasefire and destroying trust

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul addressed rumors regarding Cambodian military movements near the border. He urged the public to rely on official intelligence from the National Security Council (NSC) rather than social media trends. He declined to confirm if a 'third round' of fighting is imminent, stating he is awaiting a formal briefing. He also noted that while technical-level border committees (JBC) continue to work, high-level signings are paused as the current administration is in a caretaker role.
title: นายกฯ ขออย่าเชื่อกระแสข่าวทหารกัมพูชาเริ่มขยับ เลี่ยงตอบปะทะรอบ 3 รอ สมช.รายงาน

EOD teams have cleared 80-90% of landmines in reclaimed areas near Ban Nong Chan and Ban Nong Ya Kaeo. This has allowed 100% of local residents to return to their homes to survey damages, while the military continues to maintain security along the border line.
title: ผบ.ฉก.12 ยัน ชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา สถานการณ์คลี่คลาย ย้ำ ไม่มีความกังวล เดินหน้ารักษาอธิปไตยเต็มกำลัง

According to the Ministry of Education, over 322,000 students and 15,000 teachers are affected. While some schools in Banteay Meanchey and Koh Kong have recently reopened, educational facilities in Preah Vihear remain completely shut due to security risks and infrastructure damage.
title: Border conflict disrupts 2026 school year for 322,000 students

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul stated on Monday that Thailand will protect its sovereignty and national dignity at all costs. This comes in response to reports that Cambodia might seek international intervention regarding disputed border areas. Anutin emphasized that Thailand will not be at a disadvantage and praised the military for guarding the border during the holiday period.
title: PM Anutin Asserts Right to Protect Sovereignty Against Int'l Intervention

Key allegations include the illegal occupation of territory in four Cambodian provinces, the destruction of civilian homes, and the use of shipping containers and barbed wire to unilaterally mark borders. Cambodia stated it would not recognize any changes to the boundary resulting from military force.
title: กัมพูชา แถลง 6 ข้อ ชี้การกระทำไทย ขัดกม. ระหว่างปท. ย้ำไม่ยอมรับการเปลี่ยนเส้นแบ่งเขตแดนโดยใช้กำลัง

summary: Interior Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has instructed governors of seven provinces bordering Cambodia to remain vigilant despite the lull in fighting. The First Army Region has organized three specific areas in Sa Kaeo province (Ban Klong Phaeng, Ban Nong Chan, and Ban Nong Ya Kaeo) by placing shipping containers and barbed wire to demarcate and secure the boundary. Military engineers are also clearing landmines to allow civilians to return to their homes.

titleEn: 7 Provincial Governors Urged Not to Be Careless; Shipping Containers Placed in 3 Areas

However, the article highlights that Thai officials admitted the cause is still under investigation and argues no concrete evidence of Cambodian intent was provided.
title: Thailand accuses Cambodia over mortar incident on Thai soil, no evidence presented

Cambodia later claimed it was an 'accident' involving an exploding pile of garbage, but Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul stated Thailand has lodged a formal protest.
title: Thai Army Reports Ceasefire Violation, One Soldier Wounded

The Thai military initially accused Cambodia of violating the December 27 truce, but later stated that Cambodian counterparts claimed the incident was an 'operational error' with no intention to strike Thai territory.
title: Thai Soldier Wounded by Mortar Fire; Cambodia Calls it 'Operational Error'

summary: The Royal Thai Army, through spokesperson Maj. Gen. Winthai Suvaree, reported that a mortar round fired from Cambodia landed at Hill 469 in Ubon Ratchathani at 7:40 AM on Jan 6. One Thai soldier sustained minor shrapnel wounds. Although Cambodia claimed it was an 'operational error,' the Thai Army warned that any future mistakes will force a proportional military retaliation to protect sovereignty.
title: Thai Army Warns Cambodia to Strictly Follow Ceasefire After Mortar Incident

summary: The Second Army Region announced that a Thai soldier, Sgt. Maj. Prachya Pilachai, was injured by shrapnel from a blast in the Chong Bok area of Nam Yuen District, Ubon Ratchathani. The incident occurred despite the ongoing ceasefire, prompting immediate military reporting and investigation.
title: Army Region 2 reports blast at Chong Bok, 1 Thai soldier injured

summary: Following an explosion at Chong Bok that injured a Thai sergeant, the 2nd Army Region stated that Cambodia's letter of regret is not enough. The Thai military is demanding a concrete investigation and preventive measures to ensure such incidents, which Cambodia claimed was an 'operational error,' do not recur. Currently, the situation is reported to be under control.
title: Army Region 2: Cambodian Apology Insufficient After Soldier Injured in Blast

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul summoned top security officials after a Cambodian mortar round hit Thai territory, injuring one soldier. The condemnation follows an open letter that linked the Thai monarchy to military conflict and border disputes. The Thai Senate called the act a violation of ASEAN's non-interference principle and urged Cambodia to cease provocative comments.
title: Thai Senate Condemns Cambodian Senator for Offensive Open Letter

summary: Following a third round of military clashes, Thai children in border villages have returned to school. While Cambodian students who used to cross into Thailand are now stuck in evacuation centers due to gate closures, Thai agricultural exports remain unaffected. Local farmers are struggling to restart their livelihoods as some fields still require landmine clearance after the 'sound of gunfire' faded.
title: After 3rd Round of Clashes, Border Gates Closed but 'Thai Survival' Continues

summary: The Thai military has conducted tests on new bunker designs specifically engineered to withstand attacks from suicide drones. These fortifications are slated for construction along the border to mitigate risks from modern warfare tactics observed during the recent escalations.
title: Army Tests Anti-Drone Bunkers for Border Protection

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has ordered the Ministry of Interior to expedite financial aid for 467,128 households affected by foreign military actions at the border. A budget of 2.3 billion Baht was approved to help residents in 7 provinces including Ubon Ratchathani, Sisaket, and Sa Kaeo. The aid aims to compensate for damages caused by the conflict during late 2025 and early 2026.
title: PM Orders Rapid Relief Payments for Victims Along Thai-Cambodia Border

summary: Nearly a month after the border clashes ended, Thai forces are rapidly establishing permanent positions and infrastructure at the border. The military is focusing on securing patrol routes and bases that were 'fully retaken' following the December ceasefire agreement. The report emphasizes that under the 'stay where you are' clause of the Joint Statement, Thai troops are maintaining their presence to ensure operational safety and sovereignty.
title: Strengthening Readiness at the Frontline of Two Temples: Accelerating Internal Unity for Defense

summary: Caretaker PM and Bhumjaithai Party leader Anutin Charnvirakul campaigned in Nakhon Ratchasima, touting the government's work in reclaiming 'every disputed area' along the Thai-Cambodian border over the past four months. He stated that relations have soured, calling Cambodia 'more of an enemy than a neighbor,' and noted that border checkpoints remain closed as long as the public does not want them opened.
title: Anutin Claims Reclamation of Disputed Areas, Labels Cambodia 'More of an Enemy'

summary: The Royal Thai Army (RTA) led 23 military attachés from 20 countries, including the US, China, and Russia, to Ubon Ratchathani and Sisaket. The visit aimed to provide the 'real facts' about the border conflict. At Pha Mo E-Daeng, officials briefed the group on how Cambodian forces allegedly used Preah Vihear Temple as a military base to fire on Thai positions. The RTA emphasized that Thai counter-strikes were limited to military targets and followed international standards.
title: Thai Army Takes Military Attachés from 20 Nations to Border to Witness Evidence of Cambodian Attacks

summary: The Thai government has officially started paying 2,335 million THB in compensation to 467,128 households across 7 border provinces affected by the conflict with Cambodia. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul ordered the rapid rollout through the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation (DDPM) to alleviate suffering before upcoming elections.
title: Thai Government Begins Disbursing 2.3 Billion Baht in Border Aid

summary: The Buriram provincial government has approved over 21 million baht in aid for residents affected by clashes that began in December 2025. This includes 200,000 baht each for the families of 9 people who died during evacuations, including one volunteer security guard (Chor Bor) killed on duty. Compensation also covers injuries and agricultural damage (rice and crops) destroyed during the conflict.
title: Buriram Approves 21 Million Baht Compensation for Border Conflict Victims

summary: The Royal Thai Army (RTA) issued a strong rebuttal against Cambodian accusations. The RTA clarified three main points: that Thai infrastructure construction and the placement of Buddha statues are entirely within Thai sovereign territory. The military urged Cambodia to present facts rather than unilateral accusations that could damage the atmosphere of future cooperation.
title: Thai Army Refutes 3 Cambodian Claims, Demands End to Falsehoods Regarding Sovereignty

summary: The Royal Thai Army and Ministry of Foreign Affairs facilitated a visit by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) to Sa Kaeo, Buriram, and Si Sa Ket provinces from Jan 20-23, 2026. The visit aimed to observe the humanitarian impact on civilians affected by the military conflict. Thailand reaffirmed its commitment to international standards in caring for affected populations.
title: ICRC Team Visits Thai-Cambodia Border to Monitor Humanitarian Impact

summary: Maj. Gen. Winthai Suwaree, Thai Army spokesperson, rejected a Cambodian government statement issued on Jan 24 alleging Thai violations of sovereignty and damage to ancient sites like Ta Kwai and Preah Vihear temples. Thailand claims its military actions are self-defense and within its territory, asserting that Cambodia has lost international protection status for these sites by using them as military bases and weapon firing positions.
title: Army Denies Cambodian Claims, Affirms Thai Sovereignty in Border Operations

summary: During a political vision debate, United Thai Nation Party leader Peeraphan Salirathavibhaga stated that while the economy is a priority, the government must support the military in ending border disputes decisively. He emphasized that the Thai government must force Cambodia to compensate Thailand for losses incurred during the conflict.
title: UTN Party Leader Pushes for Military Resolution and Cambodian Reparations

summary: Lt. Gen. Paradon Pattanatabut, a PM candidate for the Thai Sang Thai party, visited Buriram province to meet with local leaders from five southern Isan provinces. He announced a proactive strategy to 'establish security along the border,' specifically the Thai-Cambodian line, to protect national sovereignty and safety. He promised to resolve long-standing land rights issues for former participants in national development (Phu Ruam Pattana Chat Thai) within three months if the party oversees security.
title: Lt. Gen. Paradon Pledges Border Security and Sovereignty Protection Under Thai Sang Thai Banner

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul addressed reports that Cambodian troops have been digging trenches near the border. He stated that the Army confirmed the activity is still far from the border and the situation is normal. He urged citizens to remain confident in their safety as the military is monitoring and controlling the area effectively.
title: Thai border remains safe after reports of Cambodian trench digging; Anutin says Army has control

summary: A naval source reported that Cambodian troops have dug trenches extending over 1 kilometer opposite Ban Sam Lang in Trat province. Additionally, Cambodian drones were detected patrolling and encroaching on the Thai side. Thailand has already filed a protest letter. While the situation is being monitored, the military maintains a defensive advantage and has not seen direct encroachment into Thai land.
title: Cambodia digs trenches near Trat, sends drones to observe Thailand

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul received reports from the Army Chief of Staff indicating that the situation on the border is normal. He clarified that the trench digging reported in Cambodia is far from the Thai border and not in the 'overlapping claims area.' The Prime Minister will visit Sa Kaeo to boost civilian confidence and verify the military's absolute control over the area.
title: PM Quells Rumors! Confirms Thai-Cambodia Border Normal

summary: Images from January 26 show Cambodian soldiers digging trenches at three locations in Pursat province, opposite Thailand's Trat province. The longest trench extends over one kilometer. Thai naval security sources confirm the activity is within Cambodian territory but noted drone surveillance flights originating from the Cambodian side. Formal protests have reportedly been lodged regarding the drones.
title: Cambodia digs trenches near Thai border by Trat province

summary: Rear Admiral Paratch Rattanachaiphan, Navy spokesperson, explained that the digging of trenches by Cambodian forces opposite Chamrak in Trat province is being done within Cambodian territory. It is not considered a provocation or a violation of the ceasefire. The Navy is monitoring the situation closely to ensure public safety and national sovereignty.
title: Navy clarifies Cambodian movements, insists no impact on Thai sovereignty

summary: Thai Supreme Commander General Ukrit Boontanont confirmed that former Cambodian Defense Minister Gen Tea Banh sent a message proposing peace talks. However, the Thai commander stated it is 'premature' to talk and that Cambodia must first prove its sincerity through actions. He also mentioned that Thailand has a 'Plan B' if the situation does not improve.
title: Cambodia Seeks Peace Talks with Thailand Through Gen Tea Banh

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul visited the border areas of Sa Kaeo province to inspect the situation and support troops at the Nanthawong operating base. During the visit, he provided financial compensation to 5 civilians who suffered from disabilities or serious injuries due to actions by external forces. He also inquired about house repairs for those affected by the conflict.
title: PM visits Ta Phraya and Ban Nong Chan, encourages troops at operating bases

summary: Prime Minister and Interior Minister Anutin Charnvirakul visited Sa Kaeo province to inspect the border. He dismissed rumors of an imminent third round of fighting, stating that the situation is normal. He explained that Cambodia's tactical trench digging is part of their own national defense strategy and not a sign of aggression. He emphasized that the Thai military is monitoring the situation closely according to the December 27, 2025 ceasefire agreement.
title: Anutin Quells Rumors! Confirms Thai-Cambodia Border Normal, Confident No Third Round of Clashes

summary: Military delegations from Thailand's 1st Army Area and Cambodia's 5th Military Region met at the Poipet International Border Checkpoint. The two-day session aims to finalize an agenda for high-level Regional Border Committee (RBC) talks scheduled for Thursday. ASEAN observers are present to monitor the proceedings following the Dec 2025 ceasefire agreement.
title: Cambodia, Thailand Begin Border Security Talks Under ASEAN Observation

summary: Prime Minister Anutin stated there is no sign of a third clash with Cambodia. He addressed reports of Cambodia digging trenches, calling it a standard defense tactic. Additionally, he mentioned he has not seen any official documents regarding rumors of Cambodia procuring more air-to-surface or air attack weaponry. He urged the public to live their lives normally as the military has the situation under control.
title: PM Insists Border is Calm, Has Not Seen Leaked Docs on Cambodia Buying Air Weapons

summary: Villagers at the Chong An Ma border in Ubon Ratchathani expressed anxiety over a potential third round of military clashes. They noted that Cambodian forces have been continuously burning grass along the border, which creates smoke that obscures surveillance visibility for Thai observers. While the Thai military maintains the situation is normal, some locals have already prepared their belongings for evacuation, citing past experiences of conflict in the area.
title: Border villagers fear 'Round 3' clash as Cambodians burn grass to mask visibility

summary: Caretaker Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul stated there are no indicators of a third round of fighting despite reports of Cambodia digging trenches near the border in Trat. He noted that military units from both sides are communicating regularly to prevent misunderstandings and are adhering to the December 27 ceasefire. Anutin visited Sa Kaeo province to assess the situation and reassured citizens that the government and military have the territory under control.
title: Anutin rules out third round of Thai-Cambodian border clashes

summary: The Royal Thai Navy clarified that the delay in paying allowances to sailors and marines stationed at the Thai-Cambodian border was due to legal processes involving the approval of the central budget. Officials confirmed that the funds have now been transferred and are being disbursed to personnel.
title: Navy explains delay in allowances for Thai-Cambodian border troops

summary: The scheduled signing ceremony between the Thai First Army Commander and the Cambodian 5th Regional Army Commander was canceled. The secretariat-level talks at the Poipet immigration checkpoint failed to resolve outstanding issues. Thai forces remain on high alert to protect sovereignty while waiting for further diplomatic mechanisms to resolve the dispute.
title: RBC meeting collapses! No agreement reached, no signing

summary: Military talks between the secretariats of the Regional Border Committee (RBC) representing the Thai First Army Region and the Cambodian 5th Regional Army ended without progress. Held in Poipet, the meeting failed to reach an agreement on the management of disputed border areas in Sa Kaeo province, specifically around Ban Nong Chan and Ban Nong Ya Kaew. No joint statement was signed today, though both sides agreed to meet again in the future.
title: Talks between Thai and Cambodian armies end in deadlock

summary: Two Thai soldiers were injured on January 30, 2026, when a grass fire at the Thai-Cambodian border ignited unexploded munitions. The incident was localized and confirmed by military officials to be an accident related to environmental conditions rather than active combat.
title: Thai Soldiers Injured in Border Munition Explosion

summary: The Regional Border Committee (RBC) meeting between Thailand's 1st Army Area and Cambodia's 5th Military Region in Poipet ended without a signed Memorandum of Agreement. Officials stated that while talks were held on January 27-28 to reduce tension, several key points remain unresolved. The Thai Army continues to maintain its sovereignty and troop presence along the border in accordance with the GBC special session statement from late 2025.
title: Thai-Cambodia RBC talks fail to reach agreement; no signing today

summary: A three-day secretariat meeting for the Regional Border Committee (RBC) between Thailand's 1st Army Area and Cambodia's 5th Military Region concluded at Poipet without an agreement. Despite discussions intended to de-escalate tensions following the December ceasefire, the two sides were unable to finalize a memorandum of agreement. Both delegations agreed to return to their headquarters for further internal discussions, though the meeting was described as a positive step for maintaining communication.
title: Thai–Cambodian Border Committee Meeting Ends with No Deal, No Signing

summary: The Secretariat of the General Border Committee (GBC) has established the 'Joint Information Center on the Thailand-Cambodia situation (JIC)' to provide accurate updates to the public and prevent the spread of misinformation. Field visits were conducted on January 20 and 26 to Chong An Ma (Ubon Ratchathani) and Ban Nong Chan (Sa Kaeo) to observe conditions firsthand.
title: Developments on Thai-Cambodian Border Situation, 30 January 2026

summary: The Royal Thai Army has invited the public to participate in a memorial ceremony on February 3, 2026, at the Army Headquarters in Bangkok. The event honors soldiers who died defending Thai sovereignty during the recent armed clashes with Cambodia. The ceremony will include a white rose laying activity and stories of bravery from the front lines.
title: Royal Thai Army to hold memorial for fallen soldiers from border conflict

summary: Thai authorities responded to Cambodian allegations that Thailand violated the ceasefire between January 12 and 22, 2026. Thailand clarified that military actions, including drone use and demining, were conducted strictly for safety and patrolling within Thai territory and do not constitute a violation of sovereignty or the ceasefire agreement. The Thai side urged the use of official channels to resolve doubts rather than public accusations.
title: Thailand Rejects Cambodian Accusations of Ceasefire Violations, Vows Adherence to GBC Framework

summary: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) expressed disappointment over Cambodia's continued use of 'distorted rhetoric' and fake news. The deputy spokesperson emphasized that Thailand is strictly following the joint statement from the December ceasefire. Thailand has established a 'Joint Information Center' to provide accurate facts and counter fake news. The MFA also rejected claims that Thailand denied visas to certain Cambodian officials, calling such reports groundless and unhelpful for de-escalation.
title: MFA Disappointed by Cambodia's Continued 'Distorted Rhetoric' Aimed at Damaging Thailand's Image

summary: During an election debate, the Pheu Thai Party proposed a diplomatic strategy to address cross-border issues with Cambodia, particularly online scam centers. The party suggested using international alliances to pressure Cambodia into cooperation on human trafficking and financial crimes. This stance comes as Thai political parties prepare for the February snap election, with border security and relations with neighbors becoming central campaign issues.
title: Pheu Thai Outlines '3D Diplomacy' to Surround Cambodia with Global Pressure to Stop Scammers

summary: On the night of Jan 30, sounds of 40mm grenade launchers and laser sightings were reported near Phupa Lek, Si Sa Ket. Thai forces fired warning shots. Commanders from both sides coordinated to resolve the issue, which was initially attributed to a lack of discipline among Cambodian local troops (Tachapana) rather than a planned attack.
title: Army Region 2 updates border situation: 40mm grenade launcher sounds heard in Kantharalak, Si Sa Ket

summary: The Chinese government has delivered the first of two planned aid shipments to Thailand, totaling 10 million yuan in value. The supplies, including blankets, folding beds, and winter clothes, are intended for Thai civilians living along the border who have been affected by the recent conflict. The delivery was received at Suvarnabhumi Airport by the Thai Minister of Defense on behalf of Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul.
title: China Sends Humanitarian Aid to Thailand for Distribution to Civilians at Thai-Cambodian Border

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul addressed reports of recent border unrest, stating that while the situation has been cleared, Cambodia should not allow such incidents to happen frequently. He emphasized that the Thai military is strong and dismissed claims that the tension was being used as a tool for political campaigning ahead of the upcoming election.
title: PM Warns Cambodia Not to 'Repeat' Border Unrest, Denies Campaign Link

summary: Thai authorities assisted 32 Thai citizens in escaping a scam compound in Cambodia. Victims revealed they were tortured if they failed to meet targets and were threatened with having their organs harvested. They managed to flee during a building raid on January 17 and sought help at the Thai embassy in Phnom Penh.
title: 32 Thais Rescued from Cambodian Call Center Scams

summary: Thai Marines arrested seven Chinese nationals attempting to enter Thailand illegally via natural border crossings in Chanthaburi. The suspects carried dozens of phones and Cambodian SIM cards, likely linked to scam operations. During border security operations, the Thai military reportedly fired warning shots after a security alarm was triggered, highlighting the high state of alert along the frontier.
title: Seven Chinese scam suspects arrested in Chanthaburi province

summary: Gen. Boonsin Padklang visited Surin province to pay respects at Prasat Ta Muean Thom and other ancient sites. He confirmed that despite recent clashes where explosives landed near military bases, the main Buddha statues at these sites remained undamaged, serving as a morale boost for troops.
title: Army Advisor Visits Border Temples, Confirms Sacred Sites Unharmed

summary: Thai media reported that Cambodian forces allegedly fired M-79 grenades at Phu Pha Lek, prompting the 2nd Army Region to retaliate. The report uses strong nationalist language, accusing the other side of 'playing unfair' during a period of fragile relations.
title: Alleged M-79 Attack at Phu Pha Lek; Thai Army Retaliates
